key_insight: Detonation-sprayed hydroxyapatite coatings improved titanium wear resistance, with the best friction and wear performance at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 3.0 and 3.3.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing the spray gas ratio could improve the durability of titanium implants operating in physiological environments.
method: Deposit hydroxyapatite on Grade 2 titanium at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 2.6–3.7.
Use X-ray diffraction to identify coating phases.
Evaluate friction and wear under dry conditions and in Ringer’s solution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports predominantly hydroxyapatite with partial α-tricalcium phosphate formation and higher wear resistance than uncoated titanium, but provides no numerical wear results.
watch_item: Improved osseointegration and long-term implant reliability require biological and durability validation beyond the reported tribological tests.
paper_title: STUDY OF TRIBOLOGICAL PROPERTIES OF BIOCOATINGS BY DETONATION SPRAYING METHOD
